artworks.title: Stormy Landscape with Pyramus and Thisbe
artworks.description: Poussin's Frankfurt stormscape dwarfs the lovers under lightning: Pyramus fallen on his sword, Thisbe discovering him as the lion flees. Ovid's mulberry tragedy becomes a classical landscape of catastrophe.

artworks.title: Pyramus and Thisbe
artworks.description: Baldung's Berlin panel sets Thisbe over the dying Pyramus beneath the fatal mulberry — German Renaissance flesh and forest framing Ovid's double suicide. Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

artworks.title: Pyramus and Thisbe
artworks.description: Cranach stages the Babylonian lovers at the spring: Pyramus already wounded, Thisbe arriving too late. Saxon court style turns the Metamorphoses episode into a cool, jewelled tragedy.

artworks.title: Pyramus and Thisbe
artworks.description: Gassel's panoramic landscape nests the mulberry rendezvous in a Flemish world-view — tiny lovers, vast hills, and the lion that started the misunderstanding. Ovid's wall-split romance as world landscape.

artworks.title: Pyramus and Thisbe
artworks.description: Gautherot's neoclassical canvas catches Thisbe's discovery of Pyramus — sword, blood, and the mulberry that will stain forever. Late-eighteenth-century pathos for Shakespeare's favourite Ovidian lovers.

popCulture.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Bottom as Pyramus — Shakespeare's mechanicals turn the Babylonian lover into the funniest tragic hero on stage.

popCulture.title: Pyramus and Thisbe
popCulture.description: The youth who loved through a wall and died under the mulberry — Ovid's template for tragic misunderstanding.
